insights.summary: The third steering committee reviewed the go-live, the budget and a proposal for phase 2. Go-live happened on 22 September, one week late because of the load test, and has gone smoothly since. Two weeks after go-live, annualised churn on the Essentielle offer is down 2.1 points, short of the 3-point target but trending well. Phase 1 has used 462,000 of its 480,000 euros, and the remaining 18,000 euros covers knowledge transfer. The committee approved phase 2 (heat-pump offers for at-risk customers, 220,000 euros, starting 2 November) subject to board approval, on the condition that Thomas Girard's team takes over running the churn model by 30 November.

decisions.decision: Phase 2 (heat-pump offer aimed at at-risk customers, estimated budget of 220,000 euros) is approved subject to board of directors approval before final commitment.
IT (DSI) approves launching phase 2 on 2 November, subject to board approval.
Running the churn model will be handed over to Thomas Girard's team by 30 November.

action_items.task: Have his team take over running the churn model.
Run two knowledge-transfer sessions with Thomas Girard's team.

risks: Launching phase 2 during winter peak periods could overload customer advisors.
Phase 2 still needs board of directors approval before final commitment.
The Essentielle churn reduction (2.1 points annualised) is still below the 3-point target.
Relying on the consulting firm for model operations in the long term is not acceptable to Customer Operations.
